sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
1. Heard Sri Arvind Srivastava III, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri G.P. Singh, learned A.G.A for the State respondents.

2. The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 20.01.2023, registered as Case Crime No. 34 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 147, 323, 504, 506 and 386 IPC, Police Station Bhojipura, District Bareilly.
Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioner in the aforesaid case.
3. Submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that petitioner is only the employee of the company and has no concerned with the offence as alleged.

It is next submitted that the present prosecution is the outcome of the earlier first information report lodged by the Director of the Mohan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167753555/
1 Company

entities.text: Mohan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sarvjeet Singh Bakshi wherein investigation is still pending and as such present criminal prosecution is absolutely mala fide in nature
and in any case the case of the petitioner is entirely different from the case of Sarvjeet Singh Bakshi.

4. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for quashing of the FIR and submitted that Sarvejeet Singh Bakshi has already been arrested in the present case and the present petitioner Mohan Singh is named in the first information report assigning the specific role and as such no interference is warranted in the present case.
5. We find substance in the argument of learned AGA.
Perusal of the impugned first information report prima facie reveals commission of cognizable offence.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others,
1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati &
another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.
